summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for June 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This report counts the packets that ARPANET hosts sent during June 1973. It separates traffic between nodes from traffic within a node and gives network totals and averages.

subtitle: BBN's table of packets output by ARPANET hosts during June 1973.

tldr.problem: ARPANET participants wanted a record of how much traffic hosts sent during June.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists output packets by host, separates inter-node from intra-node traffic, and gives monthly totals and averages.
tldr.outcome: It reports 70,245,490 inter-node packets and a 1.07 inter-node packets-per-message figure. The unit metadata says RFC 556 updates it.

today: The unit metadata says RFC 538 is updated by RFC 556. This document is a historical traffic report rather than a protocol specification.

sections.title: A June Traffic Report
sections.content: RFC 538 attaches the Host traffic statistics for June 1973. The main table is titled Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). The RFC header says it updates RFC 522.
sections.plainLanguage: The document is a monthly count of packets sent by hosts. It covers June 1973.

sections.title: Host and Site Counts
sections.content:
Each host row gives inter-node packets, intra-node packets, and their total. Site subtotals combine hosts at a site and include an average daily inter-node count and the number of days counted. Most entries count 30 days; NORSR is listed for 4 days.

The report marks BELV, ABER and LBL as having no traffic. The rows are output counts, not a description of a protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The table separates packets sent outside a node from packets sent within it. It adds host counts into site totals and reports how many days each total covers.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
The report lists 70,245,490 inter-node packets and 28,609,780 intra-node packets. Their daily averages are 2,341,516 and 953,659. The average per node-day is listed as 64,802 inter-node and 26,393 intra-node packets.

The table gives the inter-node packets-per-message figure as 1.07. ISI Host 1 has the largest inter-node count among the listed individual hosts, at 10,795,800.
sections.plainLanguage: The final lines add up traffic across the network. They show the monthly totals, daily averages, and packets per inter-node message.

references.text: RFC 522, the earlier traffic statistics report named in this RFC's header.
